message.content:
**Killing Visual Studio Code (code.exe) with `taskkill`**

| What you want | Command | Notes |
|---------------|---------|-------|
| **Kill every VS Code window** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | `/IM` matches the image name (`code.exe`). `/F` forces termination. |
| **Kill a specific instance (by PID)** | `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Use `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` to find the PID first. |
| **Kill all VS Code windows *and* their child processes** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | `/T` terminates child processes spawned by the target. |
| **Kill only VS Code windows belonging to a particular user** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq <user>"` | Replace `<user>` with the account name. |
| **Kill only VS Code windows whose title contains “Visual Studio Code”** | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "WINDOWTITLE eq *Visual Studio Code*"` | Useful if you have multiple code.exe instances and only want to close the ones with a certain title. |

### Quick‑start examples

```cmd
:: 1. Kill all VS Code instances
taskkill /IM code.exe /F

:: 2. Kill a specific instance (replace 1234 with the real PID)
taskkill /PID 1234 /F

:: 3. Kill VS Code + all its child processes
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T

:: 4. Find the PID(s) of running code.exe processes
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"

:: 5. Kill only the instance owned by user “alice”
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq alice"
```

### Using PowerShell (alternative)

If you prefer PowerShell, you can stop the process with:

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

or to target a specific PID:

```powershell
Stop-Process -Id 1234 -Force
```

---

#### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **“Access is denied”** | Run the command prompt or PowerShell as Administrator. |
| **“The process cannot be terminated”** | Some VS Code extensions may keep the process alive; try `/T` to kill child processes or close VS Code normally first. |
| **Multiple instances** | Use `/IM` to match all, or `/PID` to target a single one. |

That’s it—just drop the appropriate `taskkill` line into your CMD, batch file, or PowerShell script and VS Code will be terminated.
